scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which technically falls outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Emily Baker and I'm 75. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Ms. Baker. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find unexpected charges. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Of course. My account number is 8829-4410 and the email is emily.baker@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm the billing zip code on file and the last four digits of the payment method used?
The zip code is 90210, and the last four digits are 4492.

Thank you, Ms. Baker. I have successfully verified your account. I can see here that your service was indeed canceled 34 days ago. While our 'Standard Refund Policy' strictly limits refunds to requests made within 30 days of the charge, I can see this is your first time requesting an exception. Given your long-standing history with us, I am authorized to process a one-time courtesy refund for this transaction.
Oh, that would be wonderful. Thank you so much for understanding!

You are very welcome. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that was all I needed. Thank you for your help.
It was my pleasure, Ms. Baker. Thank you for being a valued customer. Have a wonderful day!

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and utilized a one-time courtesy exception policy to override the standard 30-day refund window, successfully issuing the refund.
